meta.title: shadow-hdk — The Shape

views.label: 1 · You call run()
views.note: Your product hands in a plan and a set of ports, then reads events as they arrive. It never waits for the end.

views.label: 2 · The plan becomes a graph
views.note: The compiler turns the plan into a graph. Every node of that graph is one governed step.

views.label: 3 · Nothing runs unjudged
views.note: Governance is asked with the effect profile before the component is called. Refuse means it is never called.

views.label: 4 · The work happens
views.note: Components do the work. The model is reached through a component, never directly by the runtime.

views.label: 5 · Two ways back to you
views.note: Events inform you; a proposal asks you to remember. The kernel is the shared vocabulary beneath all of it.

meta.subtitle: An agent runs over components you register, under a policy that judges effects rather than names.

components.label: Kernel
components.sublabel: frozen types · JSON only · depends on nothing

cards.title: What each box is
items: Host / Product — you. You own the policy, the record and the UI, and you supply the adapters
run() — the entry point you call. An async generator, so events arrive while the run is going
Compiler — turns the plan into a LangGraph graph. It compiles; it never interprets
Governed step — the single enforcement point. Every graph node is one of these
Components — everything the agent can invoke: tools, files, sandboxes, other agents
Model — whatever thinks. Reached through the agent component, never by the runtime itself

cards.title: And the ring around it
items: Governance — one function asked before every step, shown effects and context, never names
Observer — the only channel out. Eleven event kinds, fire and forget; a slow observer cannot slow a step
Sink — where a proposal lands. Your gate decides whether it becomes truth
Kernel — frozen types and protocols that everything shares and that import nothing themselves
The registry, inside the step, is the union of every component port and is refreshed every step

cards.title: How to read this drawing
items: Follow the spine left to right: you call run(), it compiles, each node is a governed step, the step invokes
Then read up: governance is consulted before any invocation happens
Then read left: events and proposals are the two ways anything comes back to you
Then read down: the kernel slab is what every layer above it depends on
Use the numbered chapters above to walk it one box at a time

cards.title: The rules this drawing encodes
items: Arrows point one way: kernel depends on nothing, runtime only on the kernel, adapters only on the runtime
No adapter imports another — each is its own installable package
Govern effects, not names: six declared fields decide policy, so a rule holds for components not yet written
Mechanism here, policy and content in your product

cards.title: The fourteen adapters that exist today
items: Thinking — langchain (every provider), acp (Codex or Claude Code driven as a component)
Doing — agent (the model loop), mcp, workspace, sandbox_subprocess, contained, derivation, devices, mqtt
Deciding — modes (a ceiling and an ask line, as data), and basic's AllowAll and Controlled
Recording — basic (stdout, file and callback sinks), otel (the run as a trace, never a payload)
Sharing — recording, which offers your live registry to a child agent as an MCP server
Adding one is a new package. None of them is a runtime change

cards.title: The counted vocabulary
items: 6 ports — model, component, governance, sink, observer, clock
6 effect fields — reads, writes, reaches, reversible, contained, costs
5 step kinds — Invoke, Await, Sequence, FanOut, Until
6 observation kinds — Completed, Refused, Asked, Failed, Pending, Acted
11 event kinds — Started, Composed, Invoked, Observed, Proposed, Refused, Asked, Spawned, Held, Spent, Ended
3 judgements, 5 end reasons, 2 postures. Each set is closed and changes only by an ADR
